paragraphs: Here's my big idea, friend: God's good promise doesn't get smaller when the giants show up. Israel stood at the edge of the land the LORD was giving them, and the scouts themselves said, "It is a good land that the LORD our God is giving us." But the people looked at the walls and the tall folks and decided the LORD hated them (Deuteronomy 1:25, 27). Fear can talk LOUD, and it will tell you the gift is a trap.

Moses answers fear with something better than a pep talk. He reminds them that the LORD "goes before you" and "carried you, as a man carries his son" (Deuteronomy 1:30-31). Then he says the sad part plain: "you did not trust the LORD your God" (Deuteronomy 1:32). Trust isn't pretending the walls aren't there. It's remembering who has been carrying you the whole way.

And look at the end, because it's a gut punch. The people said sorry, grabbed their weapons and marched up on their own, even after the LORD said, "I am not with you" (Deuteronomy 1:41-42). That's the lesson, baker: obeying LATE, on your own terms, isn't the same as trusting Him. I've sat through a long wait, so here's my plan: when God says go, I go, and when He says wait, I wait. Caleb is the one the LORD praised, because he "followed the LORD wholeheartedly" (Deuteronomy 1:36).
